evals.name: legacy-config-migration-offered
evals.expected_output: The repository has the deprecated .site-delivery/config.yaml from an earlier plugin version, and a .vf-founder-kit/config.yaml holding only docs_root and a customer-research section. Onboarding tells the founder in plain language that it found their settings in the old location and offers to copy them into the site-delivery section of .vf-founder-kit/config.yaml. Once they agree, it copies the old content in unchanged, keeps docs_root and the customer-research section exactly as they were, and shows what it wrote. It then asks whether to delete the old file and WAITS: it does not delete .site-delivery/config.yaml in the same turn as the offer, and does not delete it at all without an explicit yes.
files: .site-delivery/config.yaml with a thin-path config (tracker.kind: none, publish.kind: lovable), and .vf-founder-kit/config.yaml containing: docs_root: docs, and customer-research: root: research/customers

assertions.text: The founder is offered the migration before any file is changed, rather than it being done silently
The site-delivery section holds the old file's keys and values unchanged — nothing rewritten, defaulted, or merged in
docs_root and the customer-research section are left exactly as they were
The founder is shown what was written to .vf-founder-kit/config.yaml
The old .site-delivery/config.yaml is not deleted until the founder explicitly confirms

evals.name: fuller-path-reuses-shared-tracker
evals.prompt: Set up site-delivery. We use our GitHub board.
evals.expected_output: Finds the top-level tracker key that fk-setup wrote and reuses it: it describes the board and the human review column in plain words and asks only whether they are still right, rather than asking for the board, field and columns again. It writes the site-delivery section with stages.enabled: true and no tracker block inside it, and leaves the top-level tracker key and docs_root byte-identical.
files: .vf-founder-kit/config.yaml with docs_root: docs and a top-level tracker key (kind: github, board Delivery / Status, stage_map including human_review: Human Review), and no site-delivery section

assertions.text: The existing board and human review column are shown in plain words and only confirmation is asked for
The written site-delivery section has no tracker key
The top-level tracker key and docs_root are byte-identical afterwards
stages.enabled is true in the site-delivery section

evals.name: old-github-project-tracker-migrated
evals.expected_output: The site-delivery section has the old tracker block (kind: github-project, project, field, stage_map Brainstorm: brainstorm, Plan: plan, Implement: work, Review: review) and there is no top-level tracker key. The skill says the old block is deprecated and offers to migrate it. It copies project and field into tracker.board unchanged with kind: github, maps the Review column to human_review, and proposes stages for the other columns for the founder to confirm rather than writing them unasked. It shows what it wrote and removes the old block only after the founder confirms.
files: .vf-founder-kit/config.yaml with a site-delivery section whose tracker is the old github-project shape described in the expected output, and no top-level tracker key

assertions.text: The old tracker block is reported as deprecated and migration is offered
The migrated top-level key has kind: github
stage_map.human_review is 'Review', and board.project and board.field are copied unchanged
The other columns are proposed for confirmation, not written without asking
The old tracker block is not removed before the founder confirms

evals.name: publish-block-migrated-to-release
evals.expected_output: The site-delivery section has an old publish block (kind: supabase+lovable with supabase_project_ref <project-ref> and lovable_project_id <lovable-project-id>) and there is no top-level release key. Onboarding explains in plain words that where the site goes live is now the shared release key, and shows what it would write: branch main; supabase-migrations and supabase-functions, both with project_ref <project-ref>; then lovable with project_id <lovable-project-id>. It writes the release key and removes the publish block only after the founder confirms, and keeps every other key exactly as it was. It says delivery never deploys and that the founder releases with /core:fk-release (if they have the core plugin) or by following docs/DEPLOYMENT.md.
files: .vf-founder-kit/config.yaml with docs_root: docs, a top-level tracker key (kind: none), and a site-delivery section with schema_version 1, repo (url, main_branch: main), publish (kind: supabase+lovable, supabase_project_ref: <project-ref>, lovable_project_id: <lovable-project-id>), stages.enabled: false and the default delivery_rules; no top-level release key

assertions.text: The release key to be written is shown before anything is written, with migrations, then functions, then lovable
The release key is written and site-delivery.publish removed only after the founder confirms
release is written as a top-level key, not inside the site-delivery section
docs_root, the tracker key and every other site-delivery key are unchanged
The reply says delivery never deploys and names /core:fk-release and docs/DEPLOYMENT.md as the ways to release
